items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Sometime I'd go to Bonnie's house and we'd play in the backyard band. Next day maybe Bonnie would come to my house...

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. To get back to your very earliest days, we're going to kind of jump around, but... What did you call the neighborhood you lived in? Where you grew up?

The French Quarters. It's all part of the French Quarters. The French Settlement in North Robeson, between Annette and St. Antony. In those days, it was spread out a little more than it is now. Mm-hmm. Go ahead. That's the section there where most of what they said are Creoles were living in. Mm-hmm. And... Bonnie was about a block from me. He was on... he was on Billerish Street. And we all... Manuel Perez was right on Earthquark Street. All of it was concentrated area there.
Mm-hmm. Lots of musicians in. Lots of musicians. Who were some of the other ones that you... What were the other ones that you...

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: I can remember vividly that Boccage and those musicians played with him at West End. And so did Bonnie Bigard when Bonnie was just learning.

ctx.x: Did he have his own brass band, too?

I don't remember whether he had his own brass band or not, but I do know that he played with the major brass bands over there. And I can remember vividly that Boccage and those musicians played with him at West End. And so did Bonnie Bigard when Bonnie was just learning.
Peter Boccage is still playing and going strong.
